transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-12 16:30 UTC, duration ~54 minutes. Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Polaris CTO), Liam Chen (ML Eng), Avery Brooks (Infra).

Summary: Quick discovery re: migrating inference from their in-house vLLM/TGI setup and occasional OpenAI calls to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated or Private. Want to confirm compatibility for Mistral-based weights, match latency/accuracy, and understand security/networking for private VPC.

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? we can do a 10 minute context then go into technical.
[00:18] Maya (Polaris): maya here, hi. we're trying to reduce cloud vendor spread and get better cost predictability. currently running a mix of vLLM on-prem for low-latency and OpenAI for overflow.
[00:30] Liam (Polaris ML): liam here, i own the model infra. we've been experimenting with mistral weights. performance's okay, but we hit some odd tokenization and kv-cache differences between runtimes.
[00:45] Ethan (Redwood SE): yep, that's common. the runtime differences (vLLM vs TGI vs hosted engines) can surface kv-cache alignment and slightly different tokenization leading to prompt-level divergence.
[01:08] Avery (Infra): ava here. for us network is big — we need private endpoints in our VPC, SAML SSO, and ksm/kms for keys.
[01:20] Sofia: note we'll share our private deployment docs and SOC2 artifact later today.

[02:45] Sofia: can you outline the most critical failure modes you care about in migration?
[02:53] Maya: top priority is parity on our 'customer-facing' prompt suite — if the model drifts and hallucination increases, product ops blows up. second is latency p95/p99, we target <90ms p95 on short prompts. third is security.
[03:15] Liam: and cost — right now vLLM costs are variable but we want predictable unit economics.
[03:28] Ethan: ok. two quick lens: functional parity (same outputs for same prompts) and perf parity (latency/cost). parity isn't always exact; we focus on eval deltas that matter.

[05:30] Maya: can Redwood host Mistral 7B/13B weights directly? or do we need to convert?
[05:41] Ethan: we support the family; typically we run the same fp16/quantized formats. sometimes conversion is needed but it's automated in our model onboarding. with mistral we've seen a few tokenization tweaks for older checkpoints — we'll flag that in onboarding.
[06:02] Liam: what about runtime differences — like how vLLM handles incremental kv caching vs your runtime?
[06:12] Ethan: our runtime is optimized for continuous batching and has a KV cache abstraction. it aligns with vLLM semantics, but two caveats: (1) you might see different memory footprints depending on quantization kernels, (2) prefix caching behaviors differ for long-context workloads. we'll run a parity test with your prompt set to quantify.

[08:15] Avery: network — do you support private control plane? we can't have admin plane egress from our subnet without approval.
[08:28] Sofia: yes, Redwood Private supports a private control plane and on-prem packages. we integrate with customer KMS and can run in a VPC with no public egress for data paths. we'll send the exact architecture diagrams.
[08:44] Maya: great. do you have audit logs and admin RBAC?
[08:50] Sofia: yes SOC2 logs, per-key audit, RBAC w/ SAML. we'll attach the compliance packet.

[11:00] Liam: on evals, what's the process? we want end-to-end reproducible benchmarks.
[11:10] Ethan: we provide a benchmark template (CSV format) that captures prompt, expected output, tolerances, and metrics — latency p50/p95/p99, tokens, cost per token, and a simple hallucination score. we'll run Redwood-hosted and Dedicated, and we can help run a vLLM/TGI baseline if you provide access.
[11:35] Maya: we prefer to run baseline ourselves and share results. can you give the exact model spec and inference flags used?
[11:45] Ethan: absolutely — model version, tokenizer commit, quantization bits, and kernel flags. will include a note on sequence length padding and batching setups since they affect cost.

[13:45] Liam: we hit one issue where tokens mismatch because of special tokens added by a custom tokenizer pipeline. will Redwood's onboarding pipeline allow custom tokenizers?
[13:58] Ethan: yes, we can import custom tokenizers; we track tokenizer version in model metadata. sometimes you need a light adapter to ensure BPE merges align — we can handle that in onboarding.

[16:30] Maya: about cost, how do Dedicated pools compare? we want predictability for a 100k tokens/day workload with spikes.
[16:45] Sofia: Dedicated is reserved capacity; we can size pools based on peak qps. for 100k tokens/day with spikes to 2x, we'd propose a small 2-GPU pool or a 4-GPU burst config depending on model size and latency targets. we'll send a cost estimate.
[17:10] Avery: do you support autoscaling in Private deployments? that's important for our HA plans.
[17:20] Ethan: Private supports autoscaling with cluster policies and can preserve security posture. for on-prem we coordinate with your SREs.

[19:15] Liam: any gotchas with TGI or vLLM-exported checkpoints?
[19:25] Ethan: TGI exports are fine in most cases; vLLM tends to follow the same checkpoints but some forks can change dispatch behavior. we've seen forks that alter attention pattern implementations which impacts exact output. our onboarding includes a quick run to detect major diffs.

[22:00] Maya: can we do canary rollouts? we want staged traffic shifting between our on-prem and Redwood.
[22:12] Sofia: yes — canaries, percentage rollouts, and automatic fallback policies exist. you can route by policy (latency or cost) and set thresholds for auto-failback.
[22:30] Avery: do you persist logs or can we keep all logs on-prem?
[22:36] Ethan: we can integrate with your log ingestion; Private can forward logs to your SIEM and optionally avoid storing payloads. we have token-level cost telemetry but that can be redacted.

[24:45] Liam: curious about hallucination/regression monitoring — can Redwood alert on model quality regressions?
[24:55] Ethan: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to a prompt set. you can configure regression thresholds and get alerts when hallucination or n-gram overlap drops.

[27:30] Maya: on SLA — what uptime do you provide for Dedicated?
[27:38] Sofia: Dedicated comes with an SLA (99.95% typical) and dedicated on-call support for enterprise tiers. Private support tiers vary by contract.

[30:15] Liam: operationally, when we onboard a new model, how long till it's production-ready on Redwood?
[30:25] Ethan: typically 2-5 business days for standard models, longer if custom tokenizers or private data connectors are needed. for Mistral family it's on the faster end.

[33:00] Maya: we need to keep some workloads entirely on-prem for compliance. can we do hybrid routing?
[33:10] Sofia: yes — smart routing by policy can keep certain keys/routes pinned to private endpoints while others go to Hosted or Dedicated. fallbacks can route traffic back to on-prem if Redwood capacity is constrained.

[35:45] Liam: from a dev perspective, are your SDKs compatible with our current client wrappers? we have a wrapper that expects OpenAI-style REST.
[35:56] Ethan: Redwood API is OpenAI-esque; SDKs have compatibility modes. function calling and streaming are supported. minimal changes usually.

[38:30] Avery: security follow-ups: we need details on key rotation and HSM support.
[38:42] Sofia: we support customer-managed KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed keys in Private. key rotation and audit logs are available. we'll attach the crypto whitepaper.

[41:15] Maya: ok so the immediate next steps are: share our eval prompts, have Ethan run parity runs, get SOC docs, and schedule infra deep dive.
[41:27] Sofia: yes, and we'll also provide a sample cost model for Dedicated and Hosted to compare.

[44:00] Liam: one last technical note — we rely on streaming early tokens to reduce perceived latency. how does Redwood streaming behave vs our vLLM pipeline?
[44:12] Ethan: streaming is supported and optimized; first-token latency is usually low. differences can come from batching windows. we'll instrument with your prompt set to match your streaming heuristics.

[46:45] Maya: any blockers from Redwood side to start a pilot?
[46:50] Ethan: no blockers. we'll need your sample prompt set, a small dataset for eval, and access details if you want us to run against your vLLM baseline.

[49:30] Sofia: i'll compile the packet: SOC2, private deployment diagram, onboarding checklist, and a benchmark template. expect an email by Friday.

[52:15] Maya: thanks all. we'll coordinate internal stakeholders and get the materials over.
[52:30] Sofia: thanks, we'll follow up with proposed times for the infra deep dive and the preliminary cost estimate.

End of transcript.
